title: StageRecord
description: One stage as the document stores it.

version.description: The version of the stage's contract: which schema its settings and output follow.

depends_on.description:
The hash of the input the stage read, so staleness can be worked out on load. Absent until
the stage has run.

settings.description: The settings the stage ran with (or will run with).

output.description: What the stage returned. Absent until the stage has run.

RiverIn.description: What the river stage reads: the river inputs and the CRS they are in.

river_polygon.description: The river as water, with its islands.

crs_epsg.description:
The EPSG code of the coordinates. A geographic CRS (4326) is checked in the UTM zone of the
middle of the left bank.

mouth.description: Where chainage 0 is. Absent: the lines are used as given and the answer states no mouth.

water_profile.description:
The water level along the given centreline, by its chainage (as given, before any turning).
With `Downstream`, it says which end is lower.

end_levels_m.description:
The level of the ground (from the elevation model) at the start and at the end of the given
centreline. With `Downstream` and no water profile, it says which end is lower.

Polyline.description: A line in the project CRS: `[x, y]` points in order.

RiverPolygon.description:
The river as water: an outer ring and the islands cut out of it. A ring is a [`Polyline`] that is
closed by implication (the last point joins the first).

holes.description: Islands: each is dry land inside the shell.

Mouth.description: Where the river meets the sea, a lake or the river it flows into: where chainage 0 is.

oneOf.description: A point in the project CRS. The end of the centreline nearer to it is the mouth.

The lower end of the centreline is the mouth. The water profile or the levels at the ends
decide which end is lower.

WaterProfile.description:
The water level along a river: points sorted by chainage, read linearly between points and held
flat beyond the first and last. Two points at one chainage make a step (a weir): at that chainage
the later point holds.

WaterPoint.description:
One point of a water level profile: a river chainage and the level there, in metres. It is
written as the pair `[chainage, level]`.

centreline.description: The centreline: the one given, or the smoothed line midway between the banks.

banks.description: The banks, each turned to run the way the centreline runs; `None` unless both are given.

length_m.description: The length of the centreline in metres.

stations_checked.description: How many stations the bank checks looked at (zero without two banks).

side_fail_stations.description: How many of them failed the side check.

bank_checks.description: The stations that failed a check, in chainage order.

banks_cross.description: Where the two banks cross, if they do (the checks report it, they never repair it).

reversed.description: True when the lines were turned round so that they start at the mouth.

mouth.description: The mouth: the first point of the centreline, when a mouth was stated.

water_profile.description:
The water profile. Its chainage is from the mouth when one was stated (the profile is turned
with the line when the line is); with no mouth, it is from the start of the line as given.

Banks.description: The two banks, both running the way the centreline runs.

BankCheck.description: One station that failed a bank check.

chainage_m.description: Chainage of the station along the banks' reference line, in metres.

checks.description:
The names of the checks it failed: `side`, `missing`, `jump`, `width-wide`, `width-narrow`,
`excursion`, `crossing`.
